visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Why don't bankers value a bank with EV / EBITDA?

options.text: Banks have so much debt that EV gets enormous
Banks don't report an EBITDA figure
Deposits and interest are part of the business
Deposits count as cash, not as debt

questions.explain: For a bank, deposits are the raw material and interest is an operating cost, so the business can't be separated from its funding. Value the equity directly.
questions.explain_at: For a bank, deposits are the raw material

questions.q: A bank earns an ROE of 12%, its cost of equity is 10% and it grows 2% a year. What price to book should it trade at?
questions.explain: (ROE − g) ÷ (cost of equity − g) = (12 − 2) ÷ (10 − 2) = 1.25x. Dividing 12 by 10 forgets growth and gives 1.2x.
questions.explain_at: Price to book equals return on equity minus growth

questions.q: Safe Bank earns 120 on 1,000 of book equity and grows 2% a year. How much can it pay out in dividends?
questions.explain: To grow its loans 2%, the bank must grow its equity 2%: 20 kept back from 120 leaves 100. Treating all of net income as free cash flow ignores the capital it must hold.
questions.explain_at: Only the other one hundred can go to shareholders

questions.q: A bank trades at 0.6 times book. What's the most likely reason?

options.text: A bargain: a euro of book for sixty cents
Expected returns below its cost of equity
Its growth rate is above the market's
Too much debt on its balance sheet

questions.explain: A price below book usually means the market expects the bank to earn less than its cost of equity, or doubts the book itself. It's cheap only if returns recover.
questions.explain_at: A bank below book is usually telling you it earns less than its cost of equity

questions.q: A 7% stake in Sabadell is worth about €1.2bn. Roughly what is the whole bank worth?
questions.explain: €1.2bn ÷ 7% ≈ €17bn. Multiplying 1.2 by 7 instead of dividing gives about €8bn.
questions.explain_at: At market prices, Reuters put the stake at about one point two billion euros
